What each Livermore department spends, and who pays for it

Every one of the city's departments as a bar of the funds that pay for it. Open one to see what it spends, every fund together, and which funds pay for it, each read from the department's own two-block page in the Budget Book.

Every department

How to read this page

Each bar is a department, longest first, on the one scale the longest sets, split by the group of funds that pays for it. Click a department, or press Enter or Space on it, to open its fund groups and to show below the bars where its money comes from and where it goes, each bar naming the Budget Book page its figure was read from.

      ◇ A bar's figure is our sum of the department's funding rows in the column, not a total the city prints, and each share is ours too: a fund group's part of that sum, rounded to a tenth.

      Choose a department

      Where its money comes from

      Read from the department's Department Funding Sources block, the lower half of its page in the Budget Book (pp.85-125): one bar per fund. Each figure is one fund's share of the department, not its whole cost. The General Fund bar is the General Fund's share alone; every other bar is a fund the city keeps apart from it, wearing its fund group's colour.

      A fund marked internal service is one the city fills by charging its own departments, so the money it pays here was first charged to another department and is counted in that department's cost as well.

      Where its money goes

      Read from the department's Expenditures by Category block, the upper half of the same page: what its divisions spend under each object heading, whatever fund pays. Each figure is the whole department's cost under that heading, summed over every division the page prints under the department.

      Transfers Out is money moved to another of the city's own funds, not spent on anything, and its bar is hatched. The page prints it inside the division's total, so it is inside this side's sum too.

      How to read these bars

      Both sides are drawn on one scale, the longest bar of either filling its track. Point at a bar, or focus it, for the pages its figure was read from; the Sources and data page lists every cited page. A sum marked ◇ adds the cited bars of its side and is ours, not the city's: the page prints a department total of its own, which this site has not read as a figure, so neither sum is presented as the department's total. A share marked ◇ is ours too: one bar as a percentage of its side's sum.

      Limits on these figures: What isn't in the picture (1) · Don't add or compare these (2) · Not every year is the same kind of number (1) · Where this site, not the city, decided (3)
